content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I've connected three [product_name] modules in a network using a five-port switch. The attached diagram shows the assigned IPs. The issue is that the device with MAC E0-DC-A0-17-CC-8E sets its IP to 192.168.1.220 after each restart, even though it was configured for xxx.250. Why does it keep self-assigning xxx.220? Any ideas would be appreciated.
Is DHCP currently enabled on your network?
I suggest testing with an IP address different from *.250. Also, make sure all IPs assigned to your [product_name] devices are outside the DHCP range set on your router. Regards, [user_name]
Is it possible an old version of the program with the incorrect IP has been stored on an SD card inside your [product_name] device?
Hi [user_name], I had the same thought. If you're using an SD card, after uploading the project with the correct IP, stop the controller and save the settings to the SD card.
Hi everyone, thanks for your input. The DHCP server is enabled. Should I disable it, or select an IP outside this range? The running program is just a test, and I don't have any memory card inserted.
If DHCP is enabled, it's possible that the router or a PC is also using the same IP address as your [product_name] device.
Hello, I didn't notice the IP being occupied, but after I changed the IP of the [product_name] to a range outside of DHCP, everything now works correctly. Thanks to everyone for their help.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced a situation where a [product_name] module was automatically assigning itself an unexpected IP address after reboot, even though a static IP was manually configured. The main challenge was unclear handling of IP addresses due to DHCP being active, resulting in possible network conflicts and non-intuitive device behavior. The discussion pointed out that the device setup process does not provide clear warnings or guidance on network conflicts or DHCP settings.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] modules to consistently keep their manually set static IP addresses after reboots and to provide clear warnings if network configuration issues, such as DHCP conflicts, are detected.
